questions.question: Identify the correct form of the sentence using inversion. The committee will discuss the proposal later.
options: Only the committee will discuss the proposal later.
Later will the committee discuss the proposal.
The proposal later will be discussed by the committee.
The committee later will discuss the proposal.
questions.answer: Later will the committee discuss the proposal.

questions.question: Which option correctly uses a cleft sentence to emphasize the location? The company headquarters is in London.
options: It is in London that the company headquarters is.
London is where the company headquarters is located.
The company headquarters is located in London.
In London, the company has its headquarters.
questions.answer: It is in London that the company headquarters is.

questions.question: Select the correct formal conditional sentence expressing a hypothetical situation in the past. If the committee had reviewed the proposal, they would have approved it.
options: If the committee had reviewed the proposal, they would have approved it.
Had the committee reviewed the proposal, they would have approved it.
The committee would have approved it if they had reviewed the proposal.
The committee would have approved it, had they reviewed the proposal.
questions.answer: Had the committee reviewed the proposal, they would have approved it.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses the subjunctive mood to express a formal requirement? The committee insists that all members attend the meeting.
options: The committee insists that all members attend the meeting.
The committee insists that all members must attend the meeting.
The committee insists that all members should attend the meeting.
The committee insists that all members be attending the meeting.
questions.answer: The committee insists that all members attend the meeting.

questions.question: Identify the correct use of ellipsis in the following sentence: When did you arrive, and when will you leave? We have already discussed both.
options: We have already discussed both.
We have already discussed both of them.
We have already discussed both, haven't we?
We have already discussed both, haven't we discussed?
